title: Rebaseline pi-search against pi-web-access search behavior
description: The prior extension is the operational baseline. Research its actual OpenAI/Codex availability routing, answer/synthesis behavior, fallback policy, fetch/curator capabilities, and Pi presentation from source code and current configuration. Identify the concrete reasons pi-search feels worse, then propose a minimal parity/advantage plan before implementing. Do not run provider comparison calls or add another provider just because it exists.

logs.msg: Source review confirmed the prior pi-web-access extension auto-detects authenticated OpenAI/Codex registry models even when another model is active, preserves synthesized answers, and has broader fallback/curator/content workflows. pi-search only routes native OpenAI/Codex when active and evidence-only output is intentional. User is pausing pi-search operationally and does not want provider comparison calls; rebaseline before implementation.

User clarified the issue is not strict parity or provider ranking: even with GPT, pi-search has bugs and only technically works. Revised quality bar requires task-useful answer/citation behavior, automatic backend resolution, bounded resilience, and optional source depth; these are now open requirements rather than assumed non-goals.

User directed: save/compact, then fix design issues before implementation. Next design must cover task-useful answer/evidence output, capability-based backend resolution, bounded visible resilience, optional source enrichment, and end-to-end Pi integration tests. Preserve fetch safety/adapters unless concrete review finds defects; no provider benchmarking.

Design and implementation pass started: added typed cited provider answers, registry-driven cross-provider OpenAI/Codex resolution, one visible automatic fallback, optional bounded source enrichment through safe fetch, and Pi tool integration fixtures. Offline suite is green; live native/provider smoke remains deliberate.

Fresh installed-package Codex Pi smoke passed with concise cited output and no raw JSON. OpenRouter/DeepSeek fresh process failed before tool execution with 401 User not found, recorded as credential/session blocker. Offline 145-test suite remains green; no provider-comparison calls run.

Independent review found three P2 enrichment issues; fixed in 32c134f: UTF-8 byte bounds include fetched source content, failed enrichment counts against attempts, cancellation/deadline preserve stable search errors, and cleanup drops invalid answers. Offline check now 148 tests / 356 assertions; package refreshed.

Exa live smoke passed once (IANA domain-filtered evidence, no warnings, request id present, provider cost /bin/bash.007). Automatic routing now skips incompatible OpenAI chat-completions active models and falls through to registry/direct routing; offline check remains 148 tests / 357 assertions.
Correction: the Exa smoke provider-reported cost was $0.007; the prior log entry rendered $0 as /bin/bash due shell interpolation.
Published 61e71f9 and updated installed git package to 61e71f9. The package is active in pi; local source and main are clean/synced after the follow-up context commit.

Fresh installed-package Pi smoke passed with active Codex plus explicit provider=exa: exactly one web_search call returned three concise Markdown source links and no raw JSON. Exa adapter smoke and installed tool-path formatting are now verified; only non-native OpenRouter/DeepSeek acceptance remains blocked by 401 User not found.

2026-08-02: Reviewed official Gemini/xAI docs and current provider implementations. Model-mediated search now resolves explicit registry models; Gemini support-linked citations and xAI annotation citations are aligned; xAI X handle/date/media options, Exa date filters, official X handle/date filters, research executionModel propagation, usage-query/token accounting, and hard-constraint rejection at adapter boundaries are covered. Offline check: 165 tests / 395 assertions, TypeScript clean. No live Gemini/xAI/X requests made; live acceptance remains open.

After refreshing the installed package to 78a9af0 and restarting Pi, live smoke gates passed for active OpenAI/Codex (clean cited sources), explicit Exa (clean sources; provider cost $0.007), xAI web search with executionModel grok-4.5, xAI X search with executionModel grok-4.5, and bounded web_fetch/readability. Explicit Gemini executionModel gemini-2.5-flash reached the adapter but failed HTTP 401 because direct Google model authentication is not configured. A constrained xAI X request completed without parseable citations; retain evidence-first failure behavior until a raw provider response or reproducible no-match contract is available. Numeric xAI citation labels were exposed as titles; fixed in 33b8409, refreshed the installed checkout, and added offline coverage. Verification is now 166 tests / 396 assertions; live Gemini acceptance remains credential-blocked.

Gemini search model policy corrected: do not use legacy or full Flash/Pro models for search-only grounding. Current examples and deterministic fixtures use the Pi-available gemini-flash-lite-latest alias; runtime never silently substitutes an execution model. A corrective gemini-3.6-flash request also returned HTTP 401, confirming the direct Google auth gate; no paid Flash or Lite request was made.

After Pi reload, a direct gemini-flash-lite-latest smoke still returned HTTP 401. GEMINI_API_KEY is set in the shell and distinct from OPENROUTER_API_KEY; auth.json has no Google entry, which is normal for environment-based Google auth. Treat direct Google key validity or process resolution as the remaining blocker; no billable Gemini request was made.

Fnox profile pi was checked without exposing the secret: it resolves GEMINI_API_KEY, and a direct Google model-metadata request for gemini-flash-lite-latest returned HTTP 200. The currently running extension path still returned HTTP 401, so the key is valid and the remaining discrepancy is stale Pi process/model-registry credential state. The installed Git package is updated; full Pi restart through the fnox-backed pi wrapper is the next acceptance gate.

Reproduced the auth discrepancy safely: Google accepts the fnox key with only x-goog-api-key (HTTP 200) but returns HTTP 401 API_KEY_SERVICE_BLOCKED when Authorization: Bearer is also present. The shared model-auth helper was adding that generic bearer header to Gemini. Fixed in 18775fc, added a regression assertion, refreshed the installed checkout, and verified 166 tests / 397 assertions. Full Pi restart is required before the corrective Lite smoke.

After the 18775fc reload, Gemini Lite grounding passed with three Google sources and two provider search queries, confirming the auth-header fix. The response finished with MAX_TOKENS because the adapter's arbitrary 512-token cap was too low. Reference review found pi-web-access omits generationConfig entirely and resolves Google grounding redirect URLs with bounded HEAD requests. Raised our bounded cap to 2,048 in 22bf461; offline check remains 166 tests / 397 assertions. One post-fix live smoke and canonical URL resolution remain open.

Removed the unsupported Gemini generation cap and implemented bounded canonical resolution for Google grounding-api-redirect URLs: one HEAD lookup per known redirect source, redirect never followed automatically, original retained as sourceUrl on success and as URL on lookup failure. Offline verification is 168 tests / 402 assertions; final post-refresh Gemini smoke remains.

Saved current state: source and installed checkout are at 9ccb378; Gemini cap removal plus bounded grounding-URL cleanup are verified offline (168 tests / 402 assertions). Only one post-restart Lite smoke remains; xAI X no-citation and OpenRouter/DeepSeek 401 remain conditional/credential findings.

Final post-restart gemini-flash-lite-latest smoke passed through the installed extension: three canonical Google sources, one provider search query, no warnings, and no MAX_TOKENS. Gemini acceptance is closed; xAI X no-citation remains conditional pending a real reproduced workflow.
